sentences.text:
Author: K.Suresh Reddy
Bench: K.Suresh Reddy
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Suresh Reddy
 Criminal Petition No. 9848 Of 2023
Order:

The present criminal petition, under Section 438 Cr.P.C., is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos. 1 to 5 seeking their release on bail in the event of arrest in crime No. 383 of 2023 of Suryaraopet Police Station, N.T.R. District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 406, 420, 467 and 471 read with Section 34 IPC.

2. Heard Sri S.D.Ramachandra Rao, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners-accused Nos. 1 to 5, and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State.
3.

Case of the prosecution is that de facto complainant is Director- cum-CEO, Operations, in M.K.R.
Company, Vijayawada.
He used to do contracts in the name of the company.

In the year, 2018,
accused No. 1 approached de facto complainant and developed intimacy and informed that he used to get contracts from L & T, Bridge and Roof, and HPCL and induced him that he would provide contracts from the said companies.
Having believed the words of accused No. 1, de facto complainant accepted for the same.
Accused No. 1 also informed de facto complainant that he would provide a contract for supply of sand to Vizag Steel Plant.
Accused No. 1 collected an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- from de facto complainant by showing him a fake order.
Thereafter, in the name of Bridge and Roof Company, accused No. 1 produced two more fake orders and collected Rs.30,00,000/-, totaling to Rs.45,00,000/-.
Accused No. 1 supplied 50 trucks of sand to de facto complainant and collected an amount of Rs.1,80,00,000/-.
Accused No. 1 also collected an amount of Rs.2,70,00,000/- under the guise of supplying sand to Bridge and Roof Company.

When de facto complainant asked accused No. 1 for return of the said money, accused No. 1 postponed the same and informed de facto complainant that accused Nos. 2 to 5 are looking after the business affairs and they would provide the money.
In spite of repeated demands, no amount has been paid to de facto complainant by all the accused.
Consequently, de facto complainant gave a report to police, on the basis of which the present crime has been registered.
4. A reading of the report given by de facto complainant would show that all the allegations are attributed against accused No. 1 alone.
Even according to de facto complainant, the fake orders were created and produced by accused No. 1 alone.

In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to petitioner No. 1-accused No. 1 and the criminal petition is therefore dismissed against petitioner No. 1-accused No. 1.

sentences.text: So far as petitioner Nos. 2 to 5-accused Nos. 2 to 5 are concerned, as there is no role attributed to them, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to them.

6. Petitioner Nos. 2 to 5-accused Nos. 2 to 5 are, therefore, directed to surrender before the Station House Officer, Suryaraopet Police Station, N.T.R. District, within a period of two weeks from today.

On such surrender, petitioner Nos. 2 to 5-accused Nos. 2 to 5 are ordered to be enlarged on bail on their executing each a personal bond for Rs.50,000/- with two sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer, Suryaraopet Police Station.
After release, petitioner Nos. 2 to 5-accused Nos. 2 to 5 are directed to cooperate with the investigating agency and not to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
7. The criminal petition is accordingly allowed in part.
